version.note: The performing edition and any editorial alterations are not identified in the recording sources.

performers.note: The English ensemble name is retained as Commons gives it. It has not been normalised to the Berlin Philharmonic or a particular incarnation of the Berlin radio orchestra.

date.note: The filename says November 1959, the description says November 1956, and embedded metadata labels 1954 as ‘Date and time of digitising’. That last tag is not established as either a session date or a genuine digitisation date. The 1928 date elsewhere on Commons concerns the composition.

alternatives.value: 1954 — unexplained embedded ‘Date and time of digitising’ tag; not a verified session date.

place.note: The orchestra’s credited name does not establish a recording venue. The conflicting date information prevents a secure match to a discographic session.

matrixTakeSides.note: No matrix, take or side identification is supplied; this is not a claim that such identifiers cannot exist.

credits.note: The embedded ‘Image title’ field explicitly says ‘Audio Restoration: Pablo Varela (2015)’. This does not identify the original recording engineer.

date.note: Year attached to the named audio-restoration credit. It is distinct from the unexplained 1954 digitising tag and from the contested session years.

processing.value: Audio restoration, credited to Pablo Varela; Ogg Vorbis encoding.
processing.note: The embedded credit does not identify equalisation, noise reduction, speed correction or other restoration operations. Encoder tags name Lavf56.36.100 and Lavc56.41.100 libvorbis.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: Ogg Vorbis

composition.value: Commons applies PD-old-70 to the composition.
composition.note: The tag concerns a copyright term measured from the composer’s death. It is not a recording licence, nor a worldwide determination of composition rights.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: Commons supplies only composition-level PD-old-70; its description says November 1956, its filename says November 1959, and the dossier preserves an unexplained 1954 embedded date. All three attributions precede 1963. The opened Fricsay/RIAS commercial-carrier listing also documents French 1955 and German 1958 editions, but has not been matched to this transfer and does not settle its session. Usable under the programme’s pre-1963 European sound-recording rule; the former 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US sound-recording status is not established. A recording date alone is not represented as an independently verified first-publication date.

rights.creditLine: Maurice Ravel, Boléro; Ferenc Fricsay and ‘Berlin Symphonic Orchestra’ as credited by Commons. Audio restoration: Pablo Varela (2015). Session date disputed; recording and restoration rights not independently established. Streamed from Wikimedia Commons.
